summary: Explorer collects interactable GUI elements from a live target application and records user sessions for application-specific model training. It links repeated interface states into a navigation map that supports path planning and voice-directed interaction.

name: Breaking the Data Barrier -- Building GUI Agents Through Task Generalization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies whether mid-training on GUI perception, multimodal reasoning, and text reasoning transfers to GUI-agent planning. Experiments compare 11 task sources and curated mixtures using WebArena and AndroidWorld to investigate training-data choices when GUI trajectories are scarce.

publication.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025

name: UI-E2I-Synth: Advancing GUI Grounding with Large-Scale Instruction Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-E2I-Synth uses GPT-4o to synthesize GUI grounding instructions with varied complexity, addressing small elements, imbalanced element types, and implicit requests. The accompanying UI-I2E-Bench evaluates instruction-to-element localization across these annotation challenges.

name: TongUI: Internet-Scale Trajectories from Multimodal Web Tutorials for Generalized GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: TongUI converts multimodal online tutorials, including videos and articles, into GUI-agent trajectories. Its GUI-Net dataset contains 143,000 trajectories spanning five operating systems and more than 200 applications, and supports fine-tuning for grounding and navigation.

name: PixelWeb: The First Web GUI Dataset with Pixel-Wise Labels
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces PixelWeb, a webpage GUI dataset with element images, contours, and pixel masks. Its annotation pipeline combines bitmap channel information with DOM-based visibility and stacking analysis to address occlusion and overlapping elements.

name: WebEvolver: Enhancing Web Agent Self-Improvement with Coevolving World Model
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WebEvolver trains a co-evolving world model to predict web observations and generate additional agent-training trajectories. The same model supports look-ahead action selection at inference, with evaluation on live web-task benchmarks.

name: ScaleTrack: Scaling and back-tracking Automated GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ScaleTrack combines a unified collection of GUI grounding samples with a planning objective that predicts the next action while reconstructing prior actions. This backward prediction links the current screenshot to interaction history during agent training.

name: Leveraging Vision-Language Models for Visual Grounding and Analysis of Automotive UI
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Automotive interfaces are the primary setting; ScreenSpot is reported as a separate cross-domain evaluation.
summary: Introduces AutomotiveUI-Bench-4K and a fine-tuned vision-language model for locating elements and evaluating automotive infotainment interfaces.

name: MobileIPL: Enhancing Mobile Agents Thinking Process via Iterative Preference Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobileIPL samples trees of action-planning thoughts, propagates rule-based leaf rewards backward, and forms preference pairs for reasoning-level optimization. It also expands screenshot-based instruction data through staged evolution before evaluation on mobile GUI-agent benchmarks.

name: GUI-Shift: Enhancing VLM-Based GUI Agents through Self-supervised Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-Shift trains an inverse-dynamics task that predicts the initial action connecting two GUI states, using trajectories without natural-language instructions. It combines rule-based reinforcement learning with data filtering and evaluates transfer to Android automation and screenshot grounding.

name: Scalable Video-to-Dataset Generation for Cross-Platform Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MONDAY and an automated pipeline that extracts mobile-navigation training data from instructional videos across operating-system platforms.

name: Scaling Computer-Use Grounding via User Interface Decomposition and Synthesis
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Introduces OSWorld-G grounding evaluation and the Jedi synthesis pipeline for examples spanning layout reasoning and fine-grained interaction.

name: Efficient Agent Training for Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: PC Agent-E augments 312 human computer-use trajectories with alternative action decisions synthesized by Claude 3.7 Sonnet. It studies training with this combination and introduces WindowsAgentArena-V2 as an updated evaluation benchmark.

name: Web-Shepherd: Advancing PRMs for Reinforcing Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Web-Shepherd is a process reward model for assessing individual steps of web-navigation trajectories. It introduces a collection of 40,000 step-level preference pairs with checklists and a separate benchmark for comparing reward models, then evaluates verification during WebArena-lite navigation.

name: AutoData: A Multi-Agent System for Open Web Data Collection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces AutoData, a multi-agent system that collects web datasets from a natural-language request, and Instruct2DS, a benchmark for live collection across three domains.

publication.venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

name: GUI-explorer: Autonomous Exploration and Mining of Transition-aware Knowledge for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-explorer generates exploration goals from screenshots and interface structure, then mines observation-action-outcome triples for app-specific transition knowledge. The resulting training-free agent uses this knowledge during mobile task execution, evaluated on SPA-Bench and AndroidWorld.

name: ProgRM: Build Better GUI Agents with Progress Rewards
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ProgRM predicts per-step task completion progress to provide intermediate rewards during online GUI-agent training. It derives progress labels by using longest common subsequences to identify key trajectory steps, allowing useful partial progress to contribute even when a trajectory ultimately fails.

name: ScreenExplorer: Training a Vision-Language Model for Diverse Exploration in Open GUI World
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Trains ScreenExplorer with reinforcement learning in dynamic GUI environments, using a world-model curiosity reward and experience-stream distillation to support sustained exploration.

name: WebCoT: Enhancing Web Agent Reasoning by Reconstructing Chain-of-Thought in Reflection, Branching, and Rollback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WebCoT turns reflection, look-ahead, branching and rollback procedures into chain-of-thought training rationales. Fine-tuning on these reconstructed trajectories is evaluated for web-agent self-improvement and transfer across navigation tasks.

name: Training LLM-Based Agents with Synthetic Self-Reflected Trajectories and Partial Masking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). WebShop is one evaluation task alongside ALFWorld and SciWorld.
summary: Introduces STeP, which trains agents on synthetic trajectories containing error reflections and corrections while masking poor steps; WebShop is one of three evaluated tasks.

name: BacktrackAgent: Enhancing GUI Agent with Error Detection and Backtracking Mechanism
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: BacktrackAgent adds verification, judgment, and reflection modules to detect erroneous GUI actions and guide recovery. It develops backtracking-oriented training data that includes post-action pages and evaluates task completion and step accuracy on Mobile3M and Auto-UI.

name: UI-Genie: A Self-Improving Approach for Iteratively Boosting MLLM-based Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-Genie jointly improves a mobile GUI agent and a reward model that processes screenshots with interaction history and supplies action- and task-level feedback. Its data pipeline uses rule-based verification, corrupted trajectories, and hard negatives to support reward-guided exploration and iterative training.

name: ZeroGUI: Automating Online GUI Learning at Zero Human Cost
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines generated tasks, estimated success rewards, and online reinforcement learning to automate GUI-agent interaction training.

name: VideoCAD: A Dataset and Model for Learning Long-Horizon 3D CAD UI Interactions from Video
notes: The contribution was reviewed from the retained abstract. Sections 1 and 3 of the exact-version v2 paper identify Onshape as the browser-based interaction environment with pixel-level input.
summary: Introduces synthetic CAD interaction videos, a model for learning interface actions from video, and evaluation tasks for spatial and long-horizon reasoning.

name: Surfer-H Meets Holo1: Cost-Efficient Web Agent Powered by Open Weights
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes Surfer-H, a web agent paired with the Holo1 vision-language model family trained on web content, synthetic examples, and agent-generated data. The work introduces WebClick for web-interface localization and evaluates browser task execution on WebVoyager.

name: DPO Learning with LLMs-Judge Signal for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Uses an LLM judge to evaluate and filter synthetic GUI interaction trajectories for training a compact vision-language agent. OSWorld experiments assess the policy designed for local execution.

name: Go-Browse: Training Web Agents with Structured Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Go-Browse frames web-environment exploration as graph search so that information can be reused across data-collection episodes. It collects 10,000 successful trajectories and 40,000 interaction steps on WebArena and uses them to fine-tune a web agent.

name: GUI-Reflection: Empowering Multimodal GUI Models with Self-Reflection Behavior
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-Reflection synthesizes reflection and error-correction examples from successful trajectories and adds dedicated learning stages for these behaviors. It introduces a reflection task suite, a mobile environment for online data collection, and iterative reflection tuning.

name: UITron-Speech: Towards Automated GUI Agents Based on Speech Instructions
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UITron-Speech, which predicts GUI actions from spoken instructions and screenshots. It combines synthetic speech data and mixed-modality training with a training-free grounding refinement step.

name: AgentSynth: Scalable Task Generation for Generalist Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: AgentSynth composes easily generated subtasks into longer computer-use tasks and trajectories with adjustable difficulty. Its evaluation uses the number of subtasks to probe how agent success changes as task complexity grows.

name: GUI-Robust: A Comprehensive Dataset for Testing GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds GUI task data with real-world interaction anomalies and evaluates how agent behavior changes under those conditions.

name: Chain-of-Memory: Enhancing GUI Agents for Cross-Application Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Chain-of-Memory explicitly records action descriptions and task-relevant screen information in short- and long-term memory for GUI navigation. GUI Odyssey-CoM provides 111,000 screen-action pairs with memory annotations for learning and evaluating information retention across applications.

name: ZonUI-3B: A Lightweight Vision-Language Model for Cross-Resolution GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ZonUI-3B trains GUI grounding with a curated 24,000-example collection of mobile, desktop, and web screenshots. Its two-stage procedure first learns across platforms and then specializes on high-resolution images, with ablations on data diversity and redundant examples.

name: WebSynthesis: World-Model-Guided MCTS for Efficient WebUI-Trajectory Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its trajectory generation takes place in simulated virtual web environments.
summary: Introduces WebSynthesis, which uses a learned web world model and tree-based planning to synthesize interaction trajectories for training web agents.

name: MobileGUI-RL: Advancing Mobile GUI Agent through Reinforcement Learning in Online Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobileGUI-RL constructs an online training curriculum through agent exploration and task filtering. It adapts GRPO with trajectory-aware advantages and rewards for task completion and execution efficiency, evaluated on three online mobile-agent benchmarks.

name: Screen2AX: Vision-Based Approach for Automatic macOS Accessibility Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Screen2AX, which creates hierarchical accessibility metadata from macOS screenshots, plus datasets and Screen2AX-Task for desktop-agent evaluation.

name: FingerTip 20K: A Benchmark for Proactive and Personalized Mobile LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: FingerTip 20K gathers 20K human Android demonstrations from users' long-term everyday app use, with user context, to evaluate proactive task suggestion and preference-aware task execution.

name: Web-CogReasoner: Towards Multimodal Knowledge-Induced Cognitive Reasoning for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Web-CogReasoner separates factual and conceptual web knowledge from procedural reasoning, using a structured curriculum to train a multimodal agent. Web-CogDataset and Web-CogBench support study of these capabilities alongside web-navigation evaluation.

name: NaviMaster: Learning a Unified Policy for GUI and Embodied Navigation Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: NaviMaster trains a shared policy for GUI and embodied navigation using a common visual-trajectory formulation. It combines trajectory collection, reinforcement learning and distance-aware rewards, with evaluation across both task families.

name: MagicGUI: A Foundational Mobile GUI Agent with Scalable Data Pipeline and Reinforcement Fine-tuning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines a mobile GUI data pipeline, perception and planning capabilities, and reinforcement fine-tuning for interactive task execution.

name: VeriWeb: Verifiable Long-Chain Web Benchmark for Agentic Information-Seeking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark focuses on web information seeking and synthesis.
summary: Introduces VeriWeb, a benchmark of long-chain web information-seeking tasks with verifiable subtasks and a complete human-annotated trajectory for each task.

name: Evolving in Tasks: Empowering the Multi-modality Large Language Model as the Computer Use Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: The Self-Evolution Agent combines automatic generation of verifiable computer-use trajectories with step-wise reinforcement learning for long-horizon training. It also describes a model-enhancement procedure that integrates grounding and planning capabilities without an additional training stage.

name: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SEAgent explores unfamiliar software using a world-state assessor and an automatically generated task curriculum. It learns from failed and successful interactions through adversarial imitation and GRPO, then combines specialist experience into a generalist agent evaluated on five OSWorld software environments.

name: OpenCUA: Open Foundations for Computer-Use Agents
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents demonstration collection infrastructure, the AgentNet dataset, and a training pipeline for open computer-use models.

name: Mobile-Agent-v3: Fundamental Agents for GUI Automation
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-Owl models and Mobile-Agent-v3 orchestration, using environment-generated trajectories to support GUI capabilities.

name: A Functionality-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents in E-commerce Domains
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Amazon-Bench generates functionality-specific web tasks from page content and interactive controls, covering operations beyond product search. Its evaluator checks task completion and unintended changes to account state, such as address or purchase settings.

name: Structuring GUI Elements through Vision Language Models: Towards Action Space Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces IAML training, which augments coordinate samples to help multimodal models locate GUI elements from screen content and user instructions.

name: UItron: Foundational GUI Agent with Advanced Perception and Planning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UItron combines GUI perception and planning data engineering with supervised training and curriculum reinforcement learning in connected mobile and PC environments. It also collects more than one million operation steps across 100 Chinese apps and builds offline and online evaluation environments.

name: MobiAgent: A Systematic Framework for Customizable Mobile Agents
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Presents MobiAgent, combining MobiMind agent models, the AgentRR acceleration framework, and MobiFlow evaluation. It also introduces an AI-assisted data-collection pipeline for mobile GUI tasks.

name: OmniActor: A Generalist GUI and Embodied Agent for 2D&3D Worlds
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces OmniActor, which shares shallow model layers while separating deeper parameters to train jointly on GUI and embodied interactions. A unified action representation and mixed training data support evaluation in both task families.

name: UI-TARS-2 Technical Report: Advancing GUI Agent with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-TARS-2 combines scalable trajectory generation, stabilized multi-turn reinforcement learning, and a sandbox that supports GUI, filesystem, and terminal actions. The report evaluates the resulting agent across web, desktop, Android, and game tasks and analyzes training stability.

name: Learning Active Perception via Self-Evolving Preference Optimization for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LASER builds preference data for multi-step GUI perception by combining Monte Carlo quality estimates with region-overlap evaluation. Its self-evolving training encourages relevant region selection and adapts the amount of reasoning before predicting screen coordinates.

name: ScaleCUA: Scaling Open-Source Computer Use Agents with Cross-Platform Data
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a cross-platform computer-use dataset and agents trained with a collection pipeline combining automated interaction and human input.

name: BTL-UI: Blink-Think-Link Reasoning Model for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: BTL-UI separates GUI interaction into screen-region attention, planning and executable-command generation. It adds an automated annotation pipeline and rule-based process/outcome rewards for training, with evaluation on both static understanding and dynamic interaction.

name: GUI-ReWalk: Massive Data Generation for GUI Agent via Stochastic Exploration and Intent-Aware Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-ReWalk begins with stochastic interface exploration and then infers goals to generate coherent action trajectories. It supports long-horizon workflows across applications and studies training on the resulting data using grounding and navigation benchmarks.

name: UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability For GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UIPro pretrains GUI understanding on 20.6 million tasks and then harmonizes interaction datasets through a unified action space. Continued fine-tuning uses the merged multi-platform data to train action prediction for generalist GUI operation.

name: Mano Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The abstract reports evaluation on GUI benchmarks including Mind2Web and OSWorld.
summary: Introduces Mano, a GUI agent trained with simulated data, supervised fine-tuning, and offline and online RL, with a verification module for error recovery.

name: Orcust: Stepwise-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Orcust combines principle-constrained reward modeling with GUI trajectory collection in instrumented virtual machines. Environment-checkable and model-derived principles guide stepwise feedback for grounding, basic operations, and complete task execution.

name: UISim: An Interactive Image-Based UI Simulator for Dynamic Mobile Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Planning for agent navigation is described as a potential application of the simulator.
summary: Introduces UISim, an image-based mobile UI simulator that predicts the next screen layout after an action and renders the resulting screen for testing and data generation.

name: RISK: A Framework for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RISK combines browser-interaction training data, a benchmark, and reinforcement fine-tuning for e-commerce risk-management workflows. Its trajectories and rewards distinguish individual actions from multi-step stateful tasks involving deeply embedded web content.

name: Efficient Multi-turn RL for GUI Agents via Decoupled Training and Adaptive Data Curation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DART separates GUI reinforcement learning into asynchronous environment, rollout, data-management, and training services. It curates experience by task difficulty, successful trajectories, and step uncertainty while correcting rollout-policy mismatch, with evaluation on OSWorld.

name: Scaling Synthetic Task Generation for Agents via Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AutoPlay explores application states and functions to generate tasks, then uses a model executor and verifier to construct demonstrations. It produces 20,000 tasks across 20 Android apps and 10,000 tasks across 13 Ubuntu apps for supervised and reinforcement learning of UI agents.

name: Graph2Eval: Automatic Multimodal Task Generation for Agents via Knowledge Graphs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The framework also generates document-understanding tasks for RAG agents.
summary: Introduces Graph2Eval, which generates multimodal agent evaluation tasks from knowledge graphs, including multi-step web interactions in Graph2Eval-Bench.

name: Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The reported agent evaluations use OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.
summary: Introduces Watch & Learn (W&L), which converts human computer-use videos into UI action trajectories by predicting actions between consecutive screen states.

name: Detect Anything via Next Point Prediction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI grounding is one evaluated capability of a general visual perception model.
summary: Introduces Rex-Omni, a general visual perception model trained for coordinate prediction; GUI grounding is one capability evaluated alongside detection and OCR.

name: WebAggregator: Enhancing Compositional Reasoning Capabilities of Deep Research Agent Foundation Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The work centers on research questions and evidence aggregation across websites.
summary: Introduces WebAggregator, a pipeline for synthesizing compositional questions from websites to train deep-research agents, plus the WebAggregatorQA testbed.

name: LLMs as Scalable, General-Purpose Simulators For Evolving Digital Agent Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UI-Simulator, which generates UI states and transitions for agent-training trajectories, and UI-Simulator-Grow, which prioritizes tasks and trajectory variants.

name: GUIrilla: A Scalable Framework for Automated Desktop UI Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUIrilla systematically explores macOS interfaces to collect interaction traces and accessibility metadata for downstream GUI research. It organizes these observations into hierarchical MacApp Trees and describes an accessibility-driven collection library.

name: UltraCUA: A Foundation Model for Computer Use Agents with Hybrid Action
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UltraCUA trains a shared policy for primitive GUI actions and high-level tool calls using synthesized tasks and hybrid trajectories. Supervised fine-tuning followed by online reinforcement learning is evaluated on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.

name: AndroidControl-Curated: Revealing the True Potential of GUI Agents through Benchmark Purification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AndroidControl-Curated audits ambiguities and factual errors in AndroidControl and produces a refined evaluation dataset. The paper also studies post-training a small Magma-R1 model on a curated subset to examine the effect of data quality on GUI action assessment.

name: VideoAgentTrek: Computer Use Pretraining from Unlabeled Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Extracts structured GUI actions from screen-recorded tutorials using inverse dynamics, then uses the inferred trajectories for computer-use training.

name: Agent Data Protocol: Unifying Datasets for Diverse, Effective Fine-tuning of LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Browsing is one of several task domains covered by the protocol and its evaluations.
summary: The agent data protocol (ADP) provides a shared format for agent training data across browsing, tool use, coding, and other tasks, including web agent workflows.

name: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). WebArena is one of several environments used to evaluate this general agent training framework.
summary: DreamGym synthesizes agent experiences with a reasoning-based environment model for online RL; its evaluations include the web task setting WebArena.

name: Learning from Online Videos at Inference Time for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This work retrieves online video tutorials and converts them into structured GUI action demonstrations with short objectives. A two-stage selection process supplies a relevant local trajectory as in-context guidance at each execution step.

name: GUI-360$^\circ$: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Computer-Using Agents
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Collects Windows application trajectories with screenshots and action traces for grounding, screen parsing, and action prediction.

name: SynthAgent: Adapting Web Agents with Synthetic Supervision
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces SynthAgent, which generates tasks by exploring website elements and refines them when observations reveal conflicts. A later trajectory-refinement stage removes misaligned behavior before fine-tuning agents for the target websites.

name: AUTO-Explorer: Automated Data Collection for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Auto-Explorer, an automated GUI exploration method that records software states for training-data collection. UIXplore evaluates exploration coverage, and collected data is used to fine-tune and test GUI element grounding.

name: Grounding Computer Use Agents on Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GroundCUA turns expert desktop demonstrations into densely annotated screenshots and grounding instructions. The GroundNext model family uses this supervision and subsequent reinforcement learning, with both grounding benchmarks and an OSWorld agent configuration used for evaluation.

name: An Efficient Training Pipeline for Reasoning Graphical User Interface Agents
notes: Training compares supervised fine-tuning, chain-of-thought-augmented fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning through Group Relative Policy Optimization. The authors report that models trained on the filtered data match or surpass larger baselines.
summary: A GUI grounding pipeline filters 4.8M synthetic examples to 12K training instances and adapts a 3B vision-language model, evaluated on ScreenSpot, Multimodal-Mind2Web, and AndroidControl.

name: TaskSense: Cognitive Chain Modeling and Difficulty Estimation for GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its difficulty estimates are compared with user completion time and agent success on cognitively demanding tasks.
summary: Cognitive Chain estimates GUI task difficulty by extracting sequences of cognitive steps from execution traces, then uses those estimates to assess GUI agents.

name: Co-EPG: A Framework for Co-Evolution of Planning and Grounding in Autonomous GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Co-EPG alternates reinforcement learning for a planner with updates to a grounding model using generated training examples. The evolving grounder provides feedback to the planner, and evaluation uses Multimodal Mind2Web and AndroidControl.

name: OSGym: Scalable OS Infra for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: OSGym supplies full operating-system sandboxes with GUIs for parallel computer-use data collection and training. It combines per-replica state management, hardware-aware orchestration, copy-on-write virtual-machine disks, and layered failure recovery.

name: Fara-7B: An Efficient Agentic Model for Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces FaraGen synthetic web trajectories, a compact screenshot-based action model, and WebTailBench for underrepresented browser tasks.

name: AppSelectBench: Application-Level Tool Selection Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: AppSelectBench evaluates whether computer-using agents choose the right desktop application for a task, using generated user intents and multiple evaluation protocols.

name: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI-Agent Reliability
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces OpenApps, a configurable app ecosystem for measuring UI-agent reliability under changes in appearance and content. Its evaluation compares task success and failure behavior across many versions of the same apps.

name: GUI Exploration Lab: Enhancing Screen Navigation in Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI Exploration Lab, a simulation engine for composing screens, interface elements, and navigation graphs. It studies how supervised learning, single-turn RL, and multiturn RL affect GUI navigation and exploration.

name: WebSTAR: Scalable Data Synthesis for Computer Use Agents with Step-Level Filtering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces a pipeline that filters individual steps from noisy computer-agent rollouts and augments them with reasoning for training. WebSTAR and WebSCORE support GUI-policy supervision and a distilled process reward model, StepRM.

name: Using GUI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-EDA collects more than 2,000 screenshot-answer-action pairs from engineers working across five CAD tools and five physical domains. The accompanying benchmark evaluates more than 30 GUI agents on specialized electronic-design workflows.

name: Step-GUI Technical Report
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Step-GUI uses calibrated trajectory rewards to turn generated GUI interaction data into training signals for compact agent models. The report also introduces GUI-MCP for hierarchical GUI operations and local task delegation, and AndroidDaily for static-action and end-to-end mobile evaluation.

name: OS-Oracle: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Platform GUI Critic Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: OS-Oracle synthesizes GUI critic examples and trains a pre-action critic with supervised learning followed by consistency-preserving GRPO. It introduces OS-Critic Bench across mobile, web, and desktop settings and tests critic-assisted agents in OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

name: VenusBench-GD: A Comprehensive Multi-Platform GUI Benchmark for Diverse Grounding Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: VenusBench-GD is a bilingual, cross-platform GUI grounding benchmark organized into basic and advanced tasks. Its annotation pipeline and six-subtask taxonomy support comparisons of general multimodal models and GUI-specialized models across different grounding demands.

name: EchoTrail-GUI: Building Actionable Memory for GUI Agents via Critic-Guided Self-Exploration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: EchoTrail-GUI builds a memory of successful GUI trajectories through autonomous exploration filtered by a reward model. It retrieves relevant trajectories as in-context guidance for new tasks and evaluates the approach on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

name: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MAI-UI combines GUI navigation, native user interaction, and MCP tool calls in a family of policies trained through generated data and online reinforcement learning. The report also studies device-cloud routing and scaling of parallel environments and interaction budgets, with grounding and Android navigation evaluation.

name: ShowUI-$π$: Flow-based Generative Models as GUI Dexterous Hands
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Models discrete clicks and continuous drags with flow-based action generation, and introduces drag trajectories and the ScreenDrag benchmark.

name: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebGym supplies realistic web tasks with rubric-based evaluation and an asynchronous rollout system for reinforcement learning. It studies how training on an agent’s own interaction traces scales with task coverage and transfers to unseen websites.

name: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: InfiniteWeb generates functional, interconnected websites and task evaluators using shared specifications and task-driven development. It evaluates website construction and the transfer of GUI policies trained in these synthetic web environments to OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web.

name: From Off-Policy to On-Policy: Enhancing GUI Agents via Bi-level Expert-to-Policy Assimilation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: BEPA adapts a small set of expert GUI traces into policy-aligned guidance through trajectories reachable by the learner and a dynamically updated task cache. It evaluates this two-level approach to reinforcement learning on desktop and web benchmarks.

name: Beyond Clicking:A Step Towards Generalist GUI Grounding via Text Dragging
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The dataset and benchmark focus on dragging to select and manipulate text.
summary: GUI-Drag provides synthesized text-dragging examples, while ScreenDrag benchmarks selecting text by dragging across varied GUI contexts.

name: ShowUI-Aloha: Human-Taught GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Transforms human screen recordings and input events into annotated demonstrations used by planning and execution components for GUI tasks.

name: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MirrorGuard trains a reasoning-correction defense using GUI risk trajectories generated in a text-based neural-symbolic simulator. It evaluates whether corrections transfer to computer-use agents operating real interfaces, keeping simulated training separate from deployment tests.

name: MagicGUI-RMS: A Multi-Agent Reward Model System for Self-Evolving GUI Agents via Automated Feedback Reflux
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MagicGUI-RMS combines domain-specific and general reward models to assess GUI actions and propose corrections. A structured data pipeline and feedback-recycling process support repeated reward-model and agent improvement.

name: EvoCUA: Evolving Computer Use Agents via Learning from Scalable Synthetic Experience
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EvoCUA combines task synthesis with executable validators, asynchronous sandbox rollouts and iterative policy updates. It turns successful routines and analyzed failures into supervision and evaluates the evolving agent on OSWorld.

name: GAIA: A Data Flywheel System for Training GUI Test-Time Scaling Critic Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GAIA trains a GUI action critic on positive and negative examples, then uses that critic to collect improved examples for another training round. It studies how recycling these data affects the test-time action choices of different GUI agents.

name: SwipeGen: Bridging the Execution Gap in GUI Agents via Human-like Swipe Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SwipeGen for synthesizing varied swipe trajectories and SwipeBench for assessing their execution quality. The study examines how richer control of trajectory, speed, and timing changes GUI agents’ interaction performance.

name: OmegaUse: Building a General-Purpose GUI Agent for Autonomous Task Execution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OmegaUse combines exploratory and taxonomy-guided data synthesis with supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO for GUI control. The report introduces OS-Nav for offline Android and Ubuntu evaluation alongside established grounding and action-prediction benchmarks.

name: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DynaWeb learns a world model that predicts web-page representations after actions and uses it to generate policy-training rollouts. It interleaves these rollouts with expert trajectories and evaluates the trained web agents on WebArena and WebVoyager.

name: Learning with Challenges: Adaptive Difficulty-Aware Data Generation for Mobile GUI Agent Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MobileGen estimates a mobile agent’s strengths across structural and semantic task difficulty, then samples new training targets around that profile. A controllable multi-agent generator creates the corresponding instructions and GUI trajectories.

name: SimGym: Traffic-Grounded Browser Agents for Offline A/B Testing in E-Commerce
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported validation compares simulated results with human outcomes from UI changes on one major e-commerce platform.
summary: SimGym runs traffic-grounded synthetic buyers as browser agents to compare e-commerce storefront variants offline, using buyer profiles derived from production interactions.

name: Generative Visual Code Mobile World Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: gWorld predicts future mobile GUI states as renderable web code and supplies an automated pipeline for code-based training data. The study evaluates visual state prediction and how stronger world models affect downstream mobile policies.

name: ToolTok: Tool Tokenization for Efficient and Generalizable GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ToolTok represents GUI operations with learned tool tokens and frames interaction as progressive tool selection. Semantic anchoring and an easy-to-hard curriculum teach tool meanings before visual pathfinding, with evaluation across grounding scenarios.

name: M$^2$-Miner: Multi-Agent Enhanced MCTS for Mobile GUI Agent Data Mining
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: M2-Miner uses multi-agent-guided Monte Carlo tree search to collect mobile GUI intent–trajectory pairs. Intent recycling and progressive collector training aim to increase the diversity and usefulness of the mined interaction data.

name: ANCHOR: Branch-Point Data Generation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ANCHOR expands verified desktop demonstrations by generating new tasks at meaningful branch points and executing their instructions. State-aware verification and action filtering refine the resulting trajectories, which are evaluated through fine-tuned agents on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.

name: When Benign Inputs Lead to Severe Harms: Eliciting Unsafe Unintended Behaviors of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: AutoElicit iteratively revises benign instructions using execution feedback to surface harmful unintended actions by computer-use agents in OS workflows.

name: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs: Leveraging the Cognitive Gap for Scalable and Diverse GUI-Agent Defense
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs introduces generated interactive challenges intended to distinguish human users from GUI agents. The benchmark targets perception, memory, decisions and actions, with backend-supported challenge types designed for scalable instance generation.

name: A11y-CUA Dataset: Characterizing the Accessibility Gap in Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces A11y-CUA, a dataset comparing how blind or low-vision users and sighted users perform everyday computer tasks. It contrasts those traces with agent behavior under default, keyboard-only, and magnifier conditions to identify barriers to shared control.

name: TreeCUA: Efficiently Scaling GUI Automation with Tree-Structured Verifiable Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: TreeCUA organizes GUI exploration trajectories as reusable trees and balances deeper tasks against broader coverage. Its data pipeline combines action verification, memory-backed recovery and a DPO variant that uses information from adjacent branches.

name: Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Code2World predicts future GUI screens through renderable code, trained on AndroidCode trajectories with supervised learning and render-aware reinforcement learning. It evaluates visual prediction and downstream AndroidWorld navigation with the learned world model.

name: Autonomous Continual Learning for Environment Adaptation of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.
summary: ACuRL uses autonomous interface exploration and an adaptive task curriculum to continually train computer-use policies with reinforcement learning. CUAJudge supplies outcome feedback, and experiments study adaptation across desktop applications and environment changes.

name: LHAW: Controllable Underspecification for Long-Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: LHAW generates underspecified variants of long-horizon workflow tasks and uses agent trials to evaluate when missing information requires clarification.

name: Scaling Web Agent Training through Automatic Data Generation and Fine-grained Evaluation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This work uses constraint-based progress evaluation to retain partially successful web trajectories for training. It introduces BookingArena for structured booking tasks and studies a distilled agent trained with the resulting data.

name: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-GENESIS reconstructs applications as lightweight web environments with executable assertions for reward computation. It evaluates the cost of these training environments and transfer from synthetic interaction training to held-out real tasks.

name: ScreenParse: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ScreenParse supplies dense annotations of UI elements, types and text in web screenshots through an automated rendering and filtering pipeline. ScreenVLM learns to output structured screen markup, and the study evaluates dense parsing and transfer to GUI grounding.

name: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AutoWebWorld turns finite-state task models into interactive websites whose actions and goal states can be checked programmatically. It generates verified trajectories for training and evaluates transfer to WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web.

name: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebWorld, an open-web simulator trained on interaction trajectories for generating agent training data and testing candidate actions. WebWorld-Bench evaluates simulated transitions, alongside downstream web-agent training experiments.

name: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CowCorpus records interleaved human and agent actions during web navigation and identifies distinct patterns of user intervention. Models trained to anticipate these interventions are integrated into live web agents and assessed in a user study.

name: GUI-Libra: Training Native GUI Agents to Reason and Act with Action-aware Supervision and Partially Verifiable RL
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: GUI-Libra trains GUI agents with action-aware supervision, a curated reasoning dataset and reinforcement learning adapted to partially verifiable actions across web and mobile tasks.

name: TimeWarp: Evaluating Web Agents by Revisiting the Past
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: TimeWarp tests web agents across multiple versions of the same sites, varying visual design, frontend code and workflows. TimeTraj transfers plans across versions to collect training trajectories and study robustness to interface change.

name: WebFactory: Automated Compression of Foundational Language Intelligence into Grounded Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebFactory, a GUI-agent training pipeline that synthesizes websites, generates tasks and trajectories, and trains with decomposed rewards. Offline and online transfer evaluations examine agents trained on the generated environments.

name: WebChain: A Large-Scale Human-Annotated Dataset of Real-World Web Interaction Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebChain aligns human web-interaction trajectories with visual, structural and action data for agent training. It also introduces WebChainBench and a mid-training approach that separates spatial grounding from planning.

name: Ares: Adaptive Reasoning Effort Selection for Efficient LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). WebArena web-agent tasks are evaluated alongside tool-use and deep-research tasks.
summary: Introduces Ares, a router that selects a reasoning level for each step of a general LLM agent from its interaction history, with web agents among the evaluation settings.

name: OSExpert: Computer-Use Agents Learning Professional Skills via Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Uses GUI-based depth-first exploration to verify elementary software functions, assemble action primitives, and construct curricula of composed skills. OSExpert-Eval examines how the resulting procedural knowledge supports complex computer-use tasks.

name: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract promises a release upon acceptance.
summary: Introduces VeriEnv, which recreates websites as executable training environments and exposes internal state through a Python SDK for task generation and deterministic reward checks. Experiments examine web-agent learning across new and expanded site environments.

name: HATS: Hardness-Aware Trajectory Synthesis for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HATS, which directs GUI trajectory exploration toward semantically ambiguous actions and iteratively checks instruction-execution alignment. Feedback from trajectory refinement updates the exploration signal used to collect subsequent training examples.

name: AI Planning Framework for LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a planning taxonomy and trajectory-quality metrics for web agents, supported by 794 human-labeled WebArena trajectories and a comparison of two planning styles.

name: WebPII: Benchmarking Visual PII Detection for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebPII provides synthetic e-commerce screenshots with fine-grained annotations for sensitive information, including partially filled forms and transaction identifiers. It also trains WebRedact to detect visual PII as a privacy component for computer-use agents.

name: CAPTCHA Solving for Native GUI Agents: Automated Reasoning-Action Data Generation and Self-Corrective Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces ReCAP, a native GUI agent for interactive CAPTCHA challenges, trained with generated interaction trajectories, reasoning traces and self-correction data.

name: CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CUA-Suite combines continuous expert desktop demonstrations in VideoCUA with the UI-Vision evaluation benchmark and GroundCUA grounding data. Screen recordings, cursor traces and layered annotations support study of temporal behavior and professional software workflows.

name: UI-Voyager: A Self-Evolving GUI Agent Learning via Failed Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces a two-stage mobile GUI learner that first co-evolves trajectories and policies through rejection fine-tuning. Group Relative Self-Distillation then uses successful rollout branches to provide step-level supervision for failed trajectories, evaluated on AndroidWorld.

name: UI-Oceanus: Scaling GUI Agents with Synthetic Environmental Dynamics
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: UI-Oceanus converts autonomous GUI exploration and execution feedback into supervision for predicting future interface states. It compares forward and inverse objectives during continual pretraining and examines downstream offline and online navigation as synthetic data scales.

name: Gym-Anything: Turn any Software into an Agent Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Gym-Anything, where a setup agent configures software environments and an independent auditor checks the resulting evidence. CUA-World supplies long-horizon tasks across professional applications, with experiments on trajectory distillation and test-time auditing.

name: Structured Distillation of Web Agent Capabilities Enables Generalization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported training uses one teacher model and trajectories from six web environments.
summary: Introduces Agent-as-Annotators, which uses modular LLM roles to synthesize and filter web-agent trajectories for supervised training of a smaller web agent.

name: MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract states that artifacts will be released.
summary: Presents MolmoWebMix, combining synthetic browser trajectories, human demonstrations and GUI perception data, and MolmoWeb screenshot-to-action policies trained from it. Browser benchmarks also test parallel rollouts with best-of-N selection.

name: Turing Test on Screen: A Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agent Humanization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract focuses on detectability through touch dynamics and the trade-off with task utility.
summary: Introduces the Agent Humanization Benchmark (AHB) and mobile touch-dynamics data to assess whether GUI agents' interactions resemble human touch behavior.

name: EE-MCP: Self-Evolving MCP-GUI Agents via Automated Environment Generation and Experience Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: EE-MCP studies application-dependent mixtures of GUI actions and MCP calls using generated environments, trajectory collection and filtered training. An experience bank extracts rules from trajectory comparisons for inference-time improvement, distinct from model distillation.

name: WebForge: Breaking the Realism-Reproducibility-Scalability Trilemma in Browser Agent Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents WebForge, a pipeline that plans, generates, refines and validates self-contained interactive websites. WebForge-Bench uses these environments to evaluate browser agents across domains and controlled difficulty levels.

name: WebAgentGuard: A Reasoning-Driven Guard Model for Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebAgentGuard separates prompt-injection detection from the operating web agent through a parallel multimodal guard. The guard is trained on synthetic visual/textual examples using reasoning-focused supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.

name: From Imitation to Discrimination: Progressive Curriculum Learning for Robust Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported evaluation is on Mind2Web.
summary: Introduces the Triton dataset and a staged training curriculum for text-based web navigation agents, using hard-negative HTML examples to train element discrimination and longer task execution.

name: Towards Scalable Lightweight GUI Agents via Multi-role Orchestration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces LAMO, a training framework for a lightweight GUI agent that can execute tasks alone or serve as an action executor alongside planners in multi-agent workflows.

name: OpenMobile: Building Open Mobile Agents with Task and Trajectory Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents OpenMobile, which builds exploration-based environment memory to synthesize task instructions and switches between learner and expert policies during trajectory collection. The resulting data includes recovery behavior and is tested through mobile-agent training and benchmark-overlap analysis.

name: AutoGUI-v2: A Comprehensive Multi-Modal GUI Functionality Understanding Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AutoGUI-v2 evaluates interface functionality, grounding and predicted interaction outcomes using hierarchical regions derived through VLM-human annotation. Its tasks span multiple operating systems and expose differences between functional localization, captioning and transition-logic understanding.

name: AutoSurfer -- Teaching Web Agents through Comprehensive Surfing, Learning, and Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AutoSurfer explores website actions breadth-first, retaining page and trajectory knowledge to guide task synthesis and trajectory refinement. It evaluates the resulting training data by fine-tuning a web agent on WebArena and examining synthesized-task diversity.

name: Weblica: Scalable and Reproducible Training Environments for Visual Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Weblica, which combines HTTP-level capture and replay with website-grounded environment synthesis. The resulting interactive web environments support reinforcement learning and tests of navigation transfer and inference-time scaling.

name: LiteGUI: Lightweight GUI Agents via Multi-Solution Guided Distillation and Dual-Level Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The training framework operates on logged GUI states.
summary: LiteGUI trains lightweight GUI agents on logged states with guided on-policy distillation and dual-level RL, supported by its multi-solution Lite-Dataset.

name: How Mobile World Model Guides GUI Agents?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares mobile world models that predict state changes as delta text, full text, images or renderable code. Downstream Android benchmarks examine synthetic training trajectories and test-time guidance, including limits of post-action reflection.

name: ToolCUA: Towards Optimal GUI-Tool Path Orchestration for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ToolCUA synthesizes interleaved GUI/tool trajectories and trains agents to choose between graphical actions and higher-level tools. Staged supervised and reinforcement learning culminate in online hybrid-environment training with a reward for efficient execution paths.

name: Covering Human Action Space for Computer Use: Data Synthesis and Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces CUActSpot to evaluate clicks, drags, drawing and other screen interactions across GUI, text, tables, canvases and natural images. A renderer-based pipeline records geometry and screenshots, then generates matching instructions and action traces for training a grounding model.

name: SimPersona: Learning Discrete Buyer Personas from Raw Clickstreams for Grounded E-Commerce Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported evaluation covers held-out live storefronts and buyer behavior.
summary: SimPersona learns buyer types from clickstreams and uses persona tokens to condition web agents trained on browsing traces for live storefront tasks.

notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MementoGUI: Learning Agentic Multimodal Memory Control for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MementoGUI learns a controller for selecting, compressing and retrieving textual and region-level visual memories while leaving the GUI-agent backbone fixed. name: OpenComputer: Verifiable Software Worlds for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces OpenComputer, which builds desktop tasks around application-state verifiers and refines those verifiers using execution feedback. An evaluation harness records trajectories and assigns auditable partial credit across professional software workflows.

name: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Weasel selects web-agent training steps by balancing importance and diversity across states, sites and interaction patterns. It also prunes training accessibility trees around known action targets and regenerates rationales to match the model’s reasoning style.

name: ScaleWoB: Guiding GUI Agents with Coding Agents via Large-Scale Environmental Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Mobile, desktop and automotive interfaces are simulated as webpages.
summary: Introduces ScaleWoB, which synthesizes interactive GUI environments as backend-free webpages with verifiable rewards. Its mobile-oriented benchmark evaluates agent execution and compares selected synthetic tasks with real-app behavior.
