notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract promises future open sourcing.
summary: Presents CUA-Gym, which co-generates instructions, initial and target states, and executable reward checks through generator-discriminator iterations. Mock web applications expand training environments, with learned agents evaluated on OSWorld-Verified and WebArena.

name: Claw-Anything: Benchmarking Always-On Personal Assistants with Broader Access to User's Digital World
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Claw-Anything benchmarks persistent personal assistance across activity histories, backend services and integrated GUI/CLI interaction. Its simulated event histories introduce irrelevant or conflicting context, and a separate generation pipeline supplies training environments.

name: Scaling, Benchmarking, and Reasoning of Vision-Language Agents for Mobile GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUIEvalKit benchmarks offline navigation tasks.
summary: HyperTrack provides mobile GUI navigation tasks across Chinese apps, while GUIEvalKit benchmarks VLM agents offline and supports analysis of training scale and history.

name: MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MIRAGE constructs mobile screenshot injections in ordinary user-content regions through localization, contextual payload generation and realism curation. Its evaluation separates visual realism from attack effectiveness against pixel-observing GUI agents.

name: GUI-CIDER: Mid-training GUI Agents via Causal Internalization and Density-aware Exemplar Reselection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUI-CIDER turns GUI trajectories into textual planning and causal interface knowledge, reselects exemplars for causal structure and low redundancy, then mid-trains GUI agents on that corpus.

name: Learn from Weaknesses: Automated Domain Specialization for Small Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: LearnWeak specializes small computer-use agents by finding domain-specific weaknesses, generating targeted tasks, and training separately for planning and execution errors.

name: GTA: Generating Long-Horizon Tasks for Web Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: GTA generates multi-hop web-agent tasks and executable trajectories through crawling, retrieval, and validation, releasing a benchmark built from over 50 websites.

name: STAMP: Training Explicit Memory for Mobile GUI Agents in Controllable and Scalable Virtual Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Training uses controllable virtual environments, and evaluation is reported on Memory-World.
summary: STAMP trains explicit memory for mobile GUI agents in virtual environments by injecting facts into generated tasks and using supervised data and online RL.

name: Recovering Policy-Induced Errors: Benchmarking and Trajectory Synthesis for Robust GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: GUI-RobustEval measures how GUI agents recover from their own errors, while RoTS synthesizes recovery trajectories for training on varied failure modes.

name: PhoneWorld: From Real-App Trajectories to Dynamic and Verifiable Environments for Phone-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces PhoneWorld, which converts observed app pages, transitions and state changes into executable Android environments through a build-inspect-repair process. Generated tasks and programmatic verifiers support benchmarking, trajectory collection and online training.

name: GUI-C$^2$: Coarse-to-Fine GUI Grounding via Difficulty-Aware Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces GUI-D to score training samples by difficulty and GUI-C² to refine screen-element locations through area-gated cropping and reinforcement learning.

name: Learning to Adapt: Self-Improving Web Agent via Cognitive-Aware Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SCALE, which uses exploration roles and graph planning to train web agents, and SCALE-20k, a dataset of tasks and demonstrations from real websites.

name: BraveGuard: From Open-World Threats to Safer Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports guard evaluation on trajectory-level agent-safety benchmarks.
summary: Introduces BraveGuard, a framework that turns emerging threats and computer-use agent trajectories into training supervision for guards that monitor multi-step safety risks.

name: Context-Aware Workflow Decomposition for Automated Mobile UI Annotation Using Multimodal Large Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The experiments use expert-annotated screens from MUIAnno.
summary: Studies staged prompting for automated mobile UI element annotation, comparing workflow depths and element groupings on expert-annotated MUIAnno screens.

name: DragOn: A Benchmark and Dataset for Drag-Based GUI Interactions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DragOn supplies drag-grounding training data and a held-out benchmark for highlighting text, selecting cells, resizing elements and moving sliders. It evaluates existing vision-language models and a model fine-tuned on the drag tasks.

name: Speculative Rollback Correction for Quality-Diverse Web Agent Imitation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Speculative Rollback Correction lets a student web agent execute short branches before teacher review localizes harmful deviations. Verified continuations and localized corrections feed supervised training while an archive retains diverse successful solutions.

name: A Benchmark and Framework for Evaluating Next Action Predictions in Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a benchmark and online evaluation method for predicting the next spreadsheet action from a user's action history, using curated action sequences.

name: VISTA: View-Consistent Self-Verified Training for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: VISTA forms GRPO comparison groups from target-preserving crops of the same GUI instance with exactly remapped target boxes. A conditional, advantage-weighted cross-view anchor supplies additional supervision without entering the group baseline, and evaluation includes view-consistency robustness.

name: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ProCUA-SFT generates tasks and synthetic trajectories on live desktops seeded with document content, checking task preconditions before rollout. The resulting step-prefix examples are formatted to match inference context and used for supervised GUI-agent fine-tuning.

name: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation first lets a policy reach its own off-trajectory states, then uses skill guidance to collect successful continuations. Mixing those continuations with expert traces supplies supervision for recovery states absent from demonstrations.

name: MemGUI-Agent: An End-to-End Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agent with Proactive Context Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MemGUI-Agent makes context management an action chosen by the same policy that controls the mobile UI. Structured history, UI-state and recent-step fields are trained from annotated trajectories to retain cross-app facts while limiting context growth.

name: MobileForge: Annotation-Free Adaptation for Mobile GUI Agents with Hierarchical Feedback-Guided Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MobileForge couples real-app exploration and generated tasks with hierarchical feedback for mobile-agent adaptation. Its optimizer turns trajectory outcomes, step feedback and corrective hints into contextualized GRPO updates, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and a GUI-only MobileWorld split.

name: Automating SKILL.md Generation for Computer-Using Agents via Interaction Trajectory Mining
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Segments and clusters GUI trajectories into inspectable skills, then trains a skill-aware policy from those annotations. Its diagnostic results distinguish readable source-domain clusters from reliable transfer and report limited or absent downstream gains.

name: Fara-1.5: Scalable Learning Environments for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds browser-agent training trajectories with live and synthetic environments, solvers, user simulation, and complementary correctness and efficiency verifiers.

name: ENVS: Environment-Native Verified Search for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: ENVS branches over GUI actions in live desktop VMs, verifies successful leaves, and converts them into balanced step-level training supervision. It also introduces OSWorld-Noisy to test recovery from dynamic interruptions while retaining the underlying tasks.

name: VisCritic: Visual State Comparison as Process Reward for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: VisCritic compares before/after screenshots through change-aware visual features and an action-conditioned critic. Weakly supervised samples from existing traces train judgments of action success, progress and error type for GUI-agent verification.

name: GUI agent: Guided Exploration of User-Sensitive Screens
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: This short paper develops an explorer agent that expands from a demonstrated GUI task to discover requests likely to reach user-sensitive screens. The proposed exploration supports identifying situations where task execution should be handed back to the user.

name: WinDOM: Self-Family Distillation for Small-Model GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WinDOM obtains bounding-box supervision from a Windows 11 web reimplementation driven through Playwright, and studies rejection-sampling distillation for small GUI grounders. It treats the depth of the supervised cold start as a GRPO choice, comparing same-size EMA and larger same-family teachers.

name: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: PEEU explores web environments and turns hindsight experience into aligned high-level planning supervision. A hierarchical task-decomposition analysis examines why atomic-skill competence alone falls short of planning generalization across websites.

name: GUICrafter: Weakly-Supervised GUI Agent Leveraging Massive Unannotated Screenshots
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUICrafter first learns grounding from large collections of unannotated screenshots and webpages, then uses a smaller high-quality dataset for reinforcement-learning calibration. The curriculum targets reduced dependence on manually annotated GUI training data.

name: BaRA: Budget-constrained and Reliable Web Data Collection Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its focus is site-level data collection within an interaction budget.
summary: Introduces BaRA, a web data-collection agent that discovers live site links, checks extracted text, images, and videos, and uses history to recover from failures.

name: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Uni-GUI, a collection of executable desktop and mobile trajectories, and UI-MOPD, which trains a shared policy from its own rollouts using platform-specific teachers. The distillation procedure routes each visited state to the appropriate teacher to preserve distinct interaction conventions.

name: EvoCUA-1.5: Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-turn Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: EvoCUA-1.5 trains multi-turn desktop agents through online reinforcement learning in executable sandboxes. It combines step-level policy optimization, task filtering and calibration, an adaptive curriculum, and asynchronous rollout handling with staleness control.

name: SCALECUA: Scaling Computer Use Agents with Verifiable Task Synthesis and Efficient Online RL
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Scales computer-agent reinforcement learning through verifiable task generation, capability-aware rollout allocation, and segmented visual context.

name: HyMobileAgent: Data-Environment Co-Scaling for Efficient GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines GUI perception data, instructional videos, real and simulated devices, and planning with reflection to develop a mobile agent.

name: SEE: Structure-aware Exploring & Exploiting for Long-horizon GUI Agent Trajectory Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SEE, which first explores mobile interfaces to build a screen-and-element transition graph, then composes task trajectories through graph planning and controlled sampling. It studies coverage, loop avoidance, and transfer after training agents on the generated sequences.

name: SeekJudge: A Practical Reward Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SeekJudge, which iteratively searches and analyzes GUI trajectories to assess instruction fulfillment. The work combines dense judgment-data synthesis, a step-label benchmark, and reward-server scheduling to study accurate and practical reward feedback for agent training.

name: Scaling GUI Agents with Visual State Transitions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces State Transition Pretraining, which jointly learns to infer actions from GUI changes and predict future states from current screens and actions. Subsequent instruction-trajectory fine-tuning tests whether these representations transfer to desktop and mobile agent tasks.

name: Echoverse: Deep, Evolving Environments for Training Computer-Use Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Echoverse, which compiles specifications into stateful applications with database-grounded graders and uses rollouts to improve both the environments and agent policies. It examines behavioral depth, targeted interface practice, and environment repair as sources of training value.

name: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces OSReward and its harder and multidimensional variants for assessing judgments of computer-use trajectories. It also releases a reasoning-annotated judgment corpus and trains reward models, examining reliability, leniency bias, and evaluation cost.

name: RMSWeb: Reflection, Failure-Mode Mining, and Salvage-DS for Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported comparisons use WebVoyager, Online-Mind2Web, and WebTailBench; the abstract notes that external evaluation protocols differ.
summary: Introduces RMSWeb, a training recipe for web agents that uses reflection retries, failure-mode mining, and Salvage-DS reward and sampling methods for web actions.

name: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Qwen-CUA operates through screenshots and keyboard/mouse events while compressing older visual history into reusable context blocks. Its report combines verifiable task generation, trajectory-based training and separate browser and Bash-augmented studies.

name: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AppDeltaWorld predicts executable code updates for the next mobile UI state, using transition-constrained retrieval and rendered visual assets. It evaluates reconstruction fidelity separately from policy training and adaptation using generated environments.

name: Back to the Future: A workbook time machine for spread sheet creation benchmarks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark covers formulas, charts, pivot tables, and conditional formatting in spreadsheets.
summary: Introduces the workbook time machine to create spreadsheet-object tasks and wtmbench to evaluate spreadsheet manipulation agents using different control interfaces.

name: SynWeaver: Website-Prior Task and Trajectory Co-Synthesis for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SynWeaver explores a website to build a map of page states and executable interactions, then learns website priors for task proposals. Joint task/trajectory synthesis revises inconsistent pairs and verifies or repairs the resulting supervision.

name: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines environment-grounded training with demonstration-conditioned workflows, and introduces OSWorkerBench for extended office-task evaluation.

name: Towards Faithful Simulation of Human Shopping Behavior
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Presents RecVerse, a screenshot-based shopping simulation agent with hierarchical memory and trajectory-level RL, alongside USB, an interactive e-commerce GUI trajectory dataset.

name: Training Needs Trustworthy Worlds: Verified Synthetic Web Environments for Agent Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds synthetic websites with verified navigation, backend state, and feasible tasks to provide reliable supervision for web-agent training.

name: GSAR: Goal-State-Anchor Rewards for Mobile GUI Agents with Self-Evolving Data Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GSAR, which synthesizes GUI tasks and successful goal states, then annotates task-relevant interface elements as reward anchors. These anchors support offline trajectory verification and online policy training.

name: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces BrowserForge, which combines broad website sourcing, parallel browser sandboxes, and task-proposer/solver interaction to collect verified web trajectories. The pipeline uses page structure during synthesis but trains a policy that acts from screenshots.

name: Iron: Intent-Aligned and Retrospective Dual Learning Framework for Enhancing Generalist Virtual Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Iron, a GUI-agent training framework that aligns low-level actions with high-level intent using cycle-consistency rewards. It also repurposes failed trajectories through hindsight reconstruction and evaluates transfer to other digital tasks.

name: SIR: Self-improving Red-teaming for Compute Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SIR, which iteratively refines a reusable library of prompt-injection strategies from failed computer-use attack trajectories. Its evaluation uses deterministic system-state checks and counts attacks only when the adversarial objective and legitimate task both complete.

name: WebWorld: The Browser as a World Model for Self-Improving Web Code
notes: Adjacent browser-backed artifact validation evaluates generated artifacts and original-source recovery separately. Distinct from WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training.

name: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains discriminative web world models to distinguish the true next state from outcomes of alternative actions. Branching web trajectories support training, followed by tests of predicted-state matching, process-reward action ranking and end-to-end WebArena-Lite selection.

name: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Turns desktop applications into reproducible GUI-and-CLI environments and generates verified hybrid trajectories for agent post-training.

name: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes an online teaching framework that decides which web-agent episodes warrant a stronger teacher and which trajectory turns merit training. A solvability gate and score-guided trimming aim to preserve first-attempt performance while reducing teaching and training costs.

name: FinCUABuild: Can Agents Build Reliable Benchmarks for Dynamic Financial Computer Use?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported qualification rates are measured on FinCUABuildBench.
summary: Introduces FinCUABuildBench for assessing financial computer-use task construction and FinCUABuildAgent for generating tasks, environments, and validators.

name: BlueLM-GUI Technical Report: A Real-Device-Centric Flywheel for Self-Improving Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes a mobile-agent training pipeline centered on real-device rollouts, recovery of useful supervision from failures, and evolving evaluation tasks.

name: RankGround: Efficient High-Resolution GUI Grounding via Lightweight Reranker-Guided Crop Selection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: RankGround trains a lightweight reranker to select a promising screenshot crop before one VLM localization call. Ranking supervision uses containment and boundary-aware augmentation, with pointwise and listwise training stages.

name: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: RecreationWorld gives hybrid agents running reference applications to explore and recreate using native GUI controls and coding tools. Its multi-platform benchmark checks interaction-dependent behavior with programmatic and visual assertions, while trajectory-training transfer is evaluated separately.

name: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MintAct trains a visual-agent family for grounding, navigation and tool use across mobile, desktop and web environments. Its shared infrastructure supports trajectory collection and asynchronous online RL while controlling cross-domain sampling and off-policy drift.

name: Beyond Task Completion: Training Capable and Safe Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SCOPE, which trains computer-use agents on ordinary task demonstrations, safe continuations around hazards, and explicit refusals. Its SCOPE-Gen pipeline pairs verifiable tasks with environmental-risk variants to support joint capability and safety training.

name: MATE: Policy-Aware Security Auditing for Mobile Agents via Synthesis-Driven Trajectory Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports audits of real-device agents and results on MATEBench.
summary: Introduces MATE, a policy-conditioned auditor for mobile-agent trajectories, and MATEBench for evaluating whether those trajectories violate app security policies.

name: From Trajectories to Grounded Preferences: Process Preference Synthesis via Interaction Element Graphs for Web PRMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: HybridCUA: Learning to Orchestrate GUI and CLI for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Trains computer agents on verified GUI, command-line, and interleaved trajectories to learn when and how to combine interaction modes.

name: SimTrace: Grounded Multimodal User Trajectories Generation for Online User Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract evaluates SimTrace in an e-commerce setting.
summary: Introduces SimTrace, a framework that generates synthetic multimodal web clickstreams by pairing a computer-use client agent's actions with web observations and user context.

name: Learning Reliable GUI Agents under Imperfect Priors
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines structured GUI exploration with training designed to tolerate imperfect retrieved experience. It builds state-transition graphs and synthetic task trajectories, then injects realistic forms of interface drift so agents learn when to rely on or reject prior guidance.

name: AutoGUIWorld: Image Generators as Visual World Models for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AutoGUIWorld, which combines task planning and image editing to synthesize action-grounded GUI trajectories without running the depicted software. It filters generated transitions and tests whether training on them improves agents operating real desktop and scientific applications.

name: DeskForge: Dense Supervision from Desktop Environments for Computer-Use Agents
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Generates dense desktop supervision by varying real application scenes and combining screenshots, accessibility trees, and window geometry.

name: Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SoftwareGym: Scaling Computer-Use Agent Training with Diverse Synthesized Software Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Work2Skill: Capturing Human GUI Experience for Reusable Agent Skill Induction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Aligns human screen recordings, input events, and accessibility information to derive reusable workflow skills from desktop demonstrations.

name: ConClick: Element-Wise Contrastive Learning Improves GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Analyzes recurring distractor clicks in GUI grounding and introduces ConClick, a contrastive training method built from target–distractor pairs. Its ReClick inference procedure revisits candidate regions and compares competing predictions.

name: OpenMobile-2: Building Versatile Mobile Agents with Scalable Environments and App-Native Tools
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces OpenMobile-2, combining simulated mobile apps, emulator tasks, released training data, and policies that can alternate GUI interaction with app-native tools.

name: HyWe: Unifying Search and Operation for Real-World Hybrid Web Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces HyWe, which switches between information search and browser operation within one trajectory, alongside a demonstration pipeline and a benchmark of hybrid web tasks.

name: Glasseek: A Transparent Recipe for Training and Trustworthy Evaluation of DeepSearch Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Glasseek, a framework for deep-search agents that explore the open web, with trajectory construction, training across context compression, and a test-set leakage audit.

name: Interaction-as-a-Judge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses computer-use agents to interact with generated applications, studying whether interaction improves preference judging, requirement checks, and feedback for application generation.

name: Grounding Multimodal Large Language Model in GUI World
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2025 proceedings page and PDF; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2025 Poster. The grounding model, AssistGUIGrounder (AGG), pairs a SAM-pretrained ViT image encoder and a transformer query encoder with a two-layer box decoder. The data engine loads Common Crawl pages from 118 domains in a browser such as Chrome, scrolls them with Page Down and reads element data through UI Automation; grounding training used 0.36M web images with 22M annotations after smoothing, plus 27K mobile screenshots from WidgetCaption and RICO. ScreenSpot grounding covers mobile, desktop and web screenshots; agent fine-tuning covers MiniWob, AITW and Mind2Web. The paper gives github.com/showlab/AssistGUIGround for code and data; that repository returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-19. No arXiv version was found.
summary: Trains a 0.4B SAM-initialized GUI grounding model on 0.5M auto-collected web screenshots with 35M element annotations, then links it to a Qwen-VL planner through a position token for MiniWob, AITW and Mind2Web.

notes: In each sample, the first crop marks the grounding model's initial box and the second the box found after masking and regrounding; both are crops around the candidate. Labels come from IoU of at least 0.5 or a center point inside the ground-truth box, with box 1 chosen when both or neither qualify, so the classes are imbalanced. The card names GUIAct web data and an unnamed Windows/macOS desktop set as sources. The 12,849-sample validation split that the card and dataset_infos.json report is not in the repository at revision a09c08da, although the bundled loader expects a validation folder. Apache-2.0 is the card's data declaration and does not settle rights in the upstream screenshots. Appendix C.3 of the BAMI paper (v1 HTML) describes training its LoRA Qwen3-VL-8B corrector on 128,487 such samples.
